request: what price gives a shop the most profit?

beats.intent: Axes of price against profit with the parabola P = (p - 2)(20 - 2p) for p from 2 to 10
beats.narration: Sell at price p: each sale earns p minus two, and you sell twenty minus two p a day. Profit is their product.
beats.code:
stage.title("The best price")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 11), y_range=(0, 35), labels=("price", "profit"))
P = lambda p: (p - 2) * (20 - 2 * p)
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, P, x_range=(2, 10), color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: A tangent sliding along the curve, slope positive then zero then negative
beats.narration: Raise the price and profit climbs at first, then levels, then falls.

beats.intent: The peak at p = 6, profit 32, marked with a flat tangent
beats.narration: The peak is at a price of six, where the slope is zero: thirty two a day.
beats.code:
m = mark_point(stage, ax, 6, 32, color=RED, label="p = 6, profit 32")
flat = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(4.5, 32), ax.c2p(7.5, 32), color=RED, dashed=True)
stage.equation(r"P'(p) = 24 - 4p = 0 \Rightarrow p = 6")

request: how long does it take two pipes together to fill a pool?

beats.intent: Two bars: pipe A fills the pool in 6 hours, pipe B in 3 hours
beats.narration: Pipe A fills a pool in six hours on its own; pipe B in three.
beats.code:
stage.title("Two pipes")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [6, 3], labels=["pipe A", "pipe B"])
stage.caption("Hours to fill alone")

beats.intent: A pool rectangle filling, with A adding 1/6 and B adding 1/3 each hour
beats.narration: In one hour A fills a sixth and B a third: together, half the pool.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
pool = Rectangle(width=5, height=3, color=WHITE)
a = Rectangle(width=5, height=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7).align_to(pool, DOWN)
b = Rectangle(width=5, height=1.0, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.7).next_to(a, UP, buff=0)
stage.play(Create(pool))
stage.play(FadeIn(a), FadeIn(b))
stage.add(pool, a, b)
stage.label(a, "A: 1/6", direction=RIGHT, color=BLUE)
stage.label(b, "B: 1/3", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: A second hour filling the other half, beside 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 per hour, 2 hours
beats.narration: Half a pool an hour means the pool is full in two hours.
beats.code:
a2 = Rectangle(width=5, height=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7).next_to(b, UP, buff=0)
b2 = Rectangle(width=5, height=1.0, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.7).next_to(a2, UP, buff=0)
stage.play(FadeIn(a2), FadeIn(b2))
stage.add(a2, b2)
stage.equation(r"\tfrac16 + \tfrac13 = \tfrac12 \text{ per hour} \Rightarrow 2 \text{ hours}")

request: how do x, x^2 and 2^x grow compared with each other?

beats.intent: Axes with y = x, y = x^2 and y = 2^x from 0 to 3, the three close together
beats.narration: Near zero the three curves stay close: x, x squared and two to the x.
beats.code:
stage.title("Who grows fastest?")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 3), y_range=(0, 9))
l = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: x, color=GREEN, label="x")
q = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: x ** 2, color=BLUE, label="x^2")
e = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 2 ** x, color=RED, label="2^x")

beats.intent: Fresh axes from 0 to 8 where 2^x has pulled far ahead
beats.narration: Zoom out to eight: two to the x has shot past both.
beats.code:
ax2 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 8), y_range=(0, 260))
l2 = plot_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: x, color=GREEN, label="x")
q2 = plot_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: x ** 2, color=BLUE, label="x^2")
e2 = plot_graph(stage, ax2, lambda x: 2 ** x, color=RED, label="2^x")

beats.intent: The crossing at x = 4 where 2^x overtakes x^2 marked
beats.narration: It overtakes x squared at four, where both are sixteen, and never looks back.
beats.code:
m = mark_point(stage, ax2, 4, 16, color=YELLOW, label="(4, 16)")
stage.caption("Exponential beats any power in the end")

request: how can one graph show when a faster runner catches up?

beats.intent: Axes of seconds against metres with runner A's line starting at 20 m, 5 m/s
beats.narration: Runner A gets a twenty metre head start and runs five metres per second.
beats.code:
stage.title("Catching up")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 12), y_range=(0, 90), labels=("s", "m"))
A = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 20 + 5 * t, color=BLUE, label="A")

beats.intent: Runner B's steeper line from 0 at 7 m/s
beats.narration: Runner B starts at the line and runs seven metres per second.
beats.code: B = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 7 * t, color=RED, label="B")

beats.intent: The crossing at t = 10 s, 70 m marked beside 20 + 5t = 7t
beats.narration: B catches A where the lines cross: after ten seconds, seventy metres along.
beats.code:
m = mark_point(stage, ax, 10, 70, color=YELLOW, label="10 s, 70 m")
stage.equation(r"20 + 5t = 7t \Rightarrow t = 10")

request: what is the marginal cost of making one more item?

beats.intent: Axes of items against total cost with the curve C = 100 + 2q + 0.05q^2
beats.narration: The cost of making q items: a hundred to set up, two each, plus a bit more as the factory gets busy.
beats.code:
stage.title("Marginal cost")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 60), y_range=(0, 400), labels=("items", "£"))
Cq = lambda q: 100 + 2 * q + 0.05 * q ** 2
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, Cq, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The tangent at q = 40 with its slope 6 read out
beats.narration: The slope of the cost curve is the marginal cost: what one more item adds. At forty items it is six pounds.
beats.code:
p = mark_point(stage, ax, 40, Cq(40), color=RED, label="q = 40")
tan = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda q: Cq(40) + 6 * (q - 40), x_range=(25, 55), color=RED)

beats.intent: The curve beside C'(q) = 2 + 0.1q = 6 at q = 40
beats.narration: Differentiate: two plus a tenth of q, which is six at forty.
